figure_candidates.caption: Figure 1 . Overview of the CellWhisperer multimodal AI for natural-language analysis of transcriptome data
vlm_descriptions:
SCIENTIFIC_FIGURE

Multi-panel scientific figure describing a method called CellWhisperer for joint embedding of transcriptomes and text.

Panel a: Workflow schematic titled “Joint embedding of transcriptomes and text for data exploration via natural-language chats.” It shows a dataset of 1 million paired human transcriptomes and text. Inputs include GEO metadata, expert annotations, bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, and gene expression counts. Sample descriptions and conversations are generated using LLMs including GPT-4 and Mixtral. The central diagram shows training and inference in a 2048-dimensional multimodal embedding space, with language and transcriptome models aligned via minimized distance and supervised training. The model interface includes text prompts, answers, transcriptome embeddings, and a generative LLM component. Applications shown on the right include free-text cell labeling, user-provided transcriptome data such as single-cell RNA-seq, and chat-style querying about cell samples.

Panel b: UMAP visualization labeled “An annotated landscape of human transcriptomes.” It shows many colored clusters representing CellWhisperer embeddings of 705,430 transcriptomes from GEO. Dashed circles highlight selected regions. Biological labels connected to regions include “Activated CD8+ T Cells in Immune Response,” “Activated CD4+ T Cells in Immune Response,” “Active Myeloid Differentiation in HSPCs,” “K562 Erythroleukemia Cells in Culture,” and “Obese adipose tissue immune and metabolic state.”

Panel c: UMAP visualization titled “Querying the human transcriptome landscape with natural language.” Points are colored by CellWhisperer score for the search term “leukemia,” with a blue-to-red scale. Red regions indicate higher similarity to the leukemia query.

Panel d: Small histogram plots titled “GEO submission dates for the selected samples.” Three distributions are shown for selected biological query regions, with GEO submission dates spanning roughly 2013 to 2023.

Biological source objects visible: human transcriptomes from GEO, bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, gene expression count matrices, renal carcinoma sample metadata, immune cells, HSPCs, K562 erythroleukemia cells, adipose tissue immune/metabolic samples.

Transformations and interfaces: metadata and annotations are converted into sample descriptions and conversations by LLMs; transcriptomes and text are embedded into a shared multimodal space; natural-language prompts are used for cell labeling, sample search, and chat-based interpretation.

figure_candidates.caption: Figure 2 . Evaluation of the CellWhisperer model by zero-shot prediction of cell types, diseases, and tissues 600
vlm_descriptions:
SCIENTIFIC_FIGURE

The image is a multi-panel scientific figure about zero-shot cell type prediction for single-cell RNA-seq data.

Panel a: Workflow schematic titled “Evaluation of zero-shot cell type prediction.” A labeled scRNA-seq evaluation dataset, not used during training, is shown as a UMAP embedding with colored cell clusters and an example label “Erythrocytes.” A free-text query for cell types is passed to an evaluation module. The module shows an example query for “erythrocytes,” a UMAP colored by CellWhisperer score, and a score-density plot comparing erythrocytes as ground truth against other cell types. It indicates reclassification of cell types across multiple datasets.

Panel b: Zero-shot cell type prediction performance. Two UMAP plots compare Tabula Sapiens annotation versus CellWhisperer prediction. A confusion-matrix-like heatmap compares Tabula Sapiens annotation against CellWhisperer prediction for 20 common cell types. Visible labels include erythrocyte, macrophage, monocyte, non-classical monocyte, classical monocyte, neutrophil, basophil, NK cell, CD8-positive alpha-beta T cell, CD4-positive alpha-beta T cell, CD8-positive alpha-beta cytokine secreting effector T cell, naive B cell, memory B cell, capillary endothelial cell, type II pneumocyte, respiratory goblet cell, club cell, basal cell, and hepatocyte.

Panel c: Bar chart titled “Zero-shot performance for diverse prediction tasks.” It reports ROC-AUC and accuracy across cell type prediction and tissue/organ prediction tasks. Datasets include Tabula Sapiens, pancreas, Immgen, and a disease validation set. A random baseline is shown. Reported ROC-AUC values are high for cell type prediction, including 0.91, 0.94, 0.83, 0.99, and 0.82, while accuracy varies widely. Tissue/organ prediction results include ROC-AUC values around 0.75 and 0.87.

Panel d: Bar charts titled “Zero-shot prediction performance for selected cell attributes.” It compares ROC-AUC and accuracy for selected attributes across Tabula Sapiens cell type, Tabula Sapiens organ/tissue, and disease validation set disease subtype tasks. Random baseline lines are shown. Example queried attributes include “plasma cell,” “erythrocyte,” “kidney epithelial cell,” “tongue,” “lung,” “kidney,” “hepatocellular carcinoma,” “melanoma,” and “dilated cardiomyopathy.”

Biological source objects: single-cell RNA-seq cell embeddings, annotated cell types, tissues/organs, and disease subtype labels.

Model/interface shown: CellWhisperer zero-shot text-query interface using free-text cell type or attribute queries and producing CellWhisperer scores for cells.

Main finding shown: CellWhisperer can perform zero-shot prediction of cell types and selected biological attributes from scRNA-seq data, with ROC-AUC substantially above random baseline across multiple datasets and tasks, though accuracy depends strongly on class set and task.

vlm_descriptions:
SCIENTIFIC_FIGURE

Multi-panel scientific figure about **CellWhisperer exploration of the Tabula Sapiens dataset**.

Panel **a** shows a browser-like interface at `cellwhisperer.bocklab.org/tabulasapiens`. It includes a histogram of **CellWhisperer scores** for the text query `"structural cells with immune functions"`, a UMAP-like cell embedding colored by score, and a chat/sidebar interface. The workflow labels indicate **cell search**, **score-based selection**, **visual selection**, and natural-language chat-based querying.

Panel **b** shows a large UMAP embedding titled **Cell annotation with free-text query "structural cells with immune functions"**. Cells are colored by **CellWhisperer score**, with a blue-to-red scale ranging approximately from `-8` to `8`. Several regions are annotated with inferred cell/tissue descriptions, including **macrophages**, **endothelium**, **epithelium**, **stroma**, **pericytes**, **ciliated epithelial cells from the nasal cavity**, **endothelial cells derived from the left ventricle**, and **epithelial cells derived from the endometrium of a fertile and healthy female, specifically from the mid-luteal phase**. A dashed selected region is linked to a quoted model response identifying selected cells as **fibroblasts derived from the decidua tissue of a female individual at 10 post-conception weeks**.

Panel **c** shows a chat protocol discussing the selected cells. User prompts ask for detailed description, relevance of immune functions, and contribution of upregulated genes/pathways. The CellWhisperer answers mention **fibroblasts from decidua**, **10 post-conception weeks**, immune-related and extracellular-matrix genes including **COL1A1, COL3A1, COL1A2, MMP1, MMP2, HSP90AA1, HSPB1, HSPA1A, IFITM3, ISG15, JUN, FOSB**, and roles in tissue remodeling, immune modulation, pregnancy-associated decidual changes, and local immune response.

Panel **d** shows another UMAP titled **Mean expression of the genes mentioned by CellWhisperer**. Cells are colored by mean expression on a green-to-blue/red scale labeled **expression (log)** and **mean(mentioned genes)**. A dashed circle and arrow mark a **selected cell cluster**, corresponding to the selected cells discussed in panels b and c.

Overall, the figure presents an interactive model-assisted single-cell analysis workflow using CellWhisperer to retrieve, select, annotate, and biologically interpret cells in the Tabula Sapiens dataset based on a free-text query about structural cells with immune functions.

vlm_descriptions:
SCIENTIFIC_FIGURE

Multi-panel scientific figure about **CellWhisperer** analysis of a user-provided single-cell RNA-seq dataset.

Panel **a**: Workflow schematic titled “CellWhisperer exploration of a user-provided dataset.” It shows a user-provided dataset undergoing scRNA-seq data generation/preprocessing into an **scRNA-seq data read count matrix** in **h5ad format**, followed by an automated processing pipeline producing a **CellWhisperer-ready dataset** with genes, cells, embeddings, and cluster labels. It also shows interactive exploration options: local or web server/cloud application, with features including precomputed cluster labels, cell search, and cell chat. Example dataset is epithelial stem cells in health and inflammation, with a CellWhisperer web URL.

Panel **b**: UMAP-style embedding labeled “CellWhisperer embedding and labeling for the user-provided dataset.” Colored cell clusters are annotated with generated biological labels, including activated CD8+ T cells in intestine, cycling ileal epithelial precursor cells, active mucus-secreting goblet cells, young male ileum enteroendocrine cells, enterocytes with TMIGD1/MEP1A/GSTA1 expression, proliferating colonic or intestinal transit-amplifying cells, large intestine goblet cells, intestinal tuft cells, healthy large intestine epithelial cells, mast cells expressing inflammatory mediator genes, intestinal B cells, and erythrocytes in ileal epithelium oxygen transport.

Panel **c**: Query result visualization titled `CellWhisperer query "Show me stem cells"`. A UMAP/scatter projection is colored by **CellWhisperer score**, with a vertical color bar ranging roughly from negative blue values to high red values. Top-scoring regions appear concentrated in the upper-left area of the embedding.

Panel **d**: Chat interface panel titled “Chat protocol discussing 100 top-scoring cells for query ‘Show me stem cells’.” It shows a green prompt button: “Describe this subpopulation of cells in detail,” and a blue assistant response describing the sample as terminal ileum epithelial layer, specifically an **LGR5-expressing stem cell subpopulation**, with epithelial identity, proliferation/differentiation state, and possible immune-associated gene signal contamination or microenvironment contribution.

Panel **e**: Gene expression validation panel titled “Expression of the LGR5 gene mentioned by CellWhisperer.” A UMAP/scatter plot is colored by **LGR5 expression** on a green-to-blue scale, labeled “expression 2 (log).” LGR5 is highlighted next to the color bar, and higher expression appears in a localized region corresponding to the queried stem-cell area.

Panel **f**: Violin/boxplot comparison titled “Comparison of CellWhisperer scores for query ‘Show me stem cells’ across cell inflammation context.” It compares dataset-provided annotation categories **inflamed** and **non-inflamed** on the y-axis against **CellWhisperer score** on the x-axis. A significance bracket reports **p < 1e-37**, indicating a strong score difference between contexts.

vlm_descriptions:
SCIENTIFIC_FIGURE

The image is a multi-panel scientific figure about evaluating CellWhisperer against curated gene sets, GSVA scores, disease libraries, and dataset integration metrics.

Panel **a**: Workflow schematic titled “Evaluation of correspondence between CellWhisperer and curated gene sets.” It shows a gene set term such as “Colorectal cancer” linked to associated genes such as “CRCS6, CRCS7, …”. CellWhisperer term scoring is compared with gene set variation analysis (GSVA). The biological source objects are curated disease-associated gene sets and single-cell gene expression-derived GSVA scores. The transformation includes embedding similarity scoring by CellWhisperer and GSVA scoring for selected/reference genes. Small plots show a Pearson correlation scatterplot between “GSVA score for gene set” and “CellWhisperer score,” with Pearson correlation 0.52, and a signed KS-statistic distribution comparing CellWhisperer score negative/positive groups.

Panel **b**: Violin/box-style distributions titled “Correspondence between CellWhisperer and GSVA scores.” It reports signed KS-statistics across gene set libraries and cell types/diseases. Libraries include PanglaoDB, Augmented_2021, Tabula_Sapiens, Azimuth_2023, Disease OMIM Expanded, GO Biological Process 2023, and GO Molecular Function 2023. A table-like column reports the number of significant terms, e.g. 164 of 178, 403 of 469, 1279 of 1425, 142 of 187, 4083 of 5406, and 792 of 1147. The finding shown is mostly positive correspondence between CellWhisperer and GSVA scores.

Panel **c**: Plot titled “Correlations for disease library.” It shows cumulative proportion versus correlation coefficient rho for n=187 disease terms. Labeled examples include “colorectal cancer,” “thyroid carcinoma,” “nephropathy,” “stature,” and “dyslexia.” The curve indicates many disease-library terms have positive correlations, with annotated high-positive examples near the upper right.

Panel **d**: Evaluation of dataset integration performance. Two schematic metric panels compare CellWhisperer and Geneformer. The left panel is “Batch integration score,” showing low/poor versus high/good batch mixing using colored cell clusters labeled Batch 1, Batch 2, Batch 3; the bar chart reports CellWhisperer 0.84 and Geneformer 0.78. The right panel is “Cell type clustering score,” showing low/poor versus high/good separation of cell types labeled cell type 1, 2, and 3; the bar chart reports CellWhisperer 0.56 and Geneformer 0.49.

Overall finding: the figure presents CellWhisperer as producing text/gene-set scores that correspond positively with GSVA-derived biological signatures and as outperforming Geneformer on the shown batch integration and cell type clustering metrics.
